title: Reliance-graph pipeline project structure descriptor
description: Stage P0 input contract (plan.md §1.1). One per project workspace. Every later stage reads this instead of hardcoding project shape.

name.description: Project identifier, used as a namespace prefix in generated artifact paths.

crate_naming_convention.description: This project's own crate/package naming rule, prose or regex (e.g. '^myproj-[a-z]+'). Never hardcoded by the pipeline itself -- see docs/concept-to-code-modifications.md gap #4.

mode.description: greenfield = Mode R, requirements-governed decomposition (plan.md §11). port = Mode P, a foreign-language source port validated by differential testing against an oracle.

port_source.description: Required when mode == 'port'; absent when mode == 'greenfield'.

repository.description: Path or URL to the source-of-truth repository being ported (e.g. the C++ project).

language.description: Origin language, e.g. 'cpp'. Recorded here, not in concept-to-code's schema -- see docs/concept-to-code-modifications.md gap #3.

oracle_build_command.description: Command that builds/runs the origin-language oracle used for Mode P differential testing (plan.md §11).

crates.description: concept-to-code binding per crate -- replaces ad hoc --crate-dir/--contracts-crate/--specs-search-root flags (docs/concept-to-code-modifications.md gap #1).

crate_dir.description: Path (workspace-relative) to the crate root containing src/ and tests/.

contracts_crate.description: Name of the verifier-contracts facade crate this crate's generated stubs depend on.

specs_search_root.description: Root directory searched for another crate's spec JSON when resolving implements/trait_ref/variants.

verifier_policy.description: Which verifier system owns which cluster (plan.md §4). CLOSED -- exactly three keys: 'default' (required), 'clusters', and 'supporting'. This was the descriptor's only open object until chainlink #104, where 'additionalProperties: {$ref: verifier}' made the whole rule 'any key name, as long as its value is a member of the verifier enum'. That made a misspelling ('defualt', 'fallback') indistinguishable from a real per-cluster override: {"default": "creusot", "defualt": "kani"} validated as an override for a cluster literally named 'defualt', 'check' exited 0 with no findings, and nothing would ever read it. Per-cluster overrides live under 'clusters' instead, where a key is either a cluster name or a typo of one, and 'clusters' constrains its own keys with the same ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$ pattern every cluster name in this pipeline already follows (docs/closure-profile-schema.json, schemas/project-state.schema.json) -- so a key that could not name a cluster at all is rejected at load instead of waiting forever to be read. 'supporting' is the declared shape for a second or supporting verifier whose evidence backs the primary one (e.g. a deductive cluster with a model-checking fallback); order is not significant, duplicates are permitted but meaningless. Every value is a member of the verifier enum.

default.description: The verifier for every cluster not listed under 'clusters'. Required: without it no cluster has an owner.

clusters.description: Per-cluster verifier overrides, keyed by cluster name -- the documented home for what used to be arbitrary sibling keys of 'default' (chainlink #104). A cluster not listed here uses 'default'; a key that names no cluster in the workspace is simply never read, which is why the key pattern below is enforced rather than left to convention. Optional and absent by default: a single-verifier project declares only 'default'.

supporting.description: Additional verifiers whose evidence supports the primary one (chainlink #76) -- the real shape for multi-verifier composition, replacing the accident of an arbitrary extra key holding a second enum member (which validated while nothing ever read it). Order is not significant; duplicates are permitted but meaningless.

closure_kind.description: The project's intended closure_kind for its clusters, declared before any code exists (chainlink #73). plan.md §4's vocabulary: deductive = Creusot/Verus-owned (universal over inputs, modulo SMT completeness and trusted specs); bounded = Kani-owned (holds only within unwind/harness bounds and enumerated monomorphizations); partial = partially verified (chainlink #85) -- a pilot that knows it cannot achieve full deductive closure may declare that intent here instead of being limited to the two uniform claims its clusters can only round to. This records intent only -- each cluster's closure profile (specs/_closure/<cluster>.json) remains the authoritative per-cluster declaration at Stage 8C, and gate g14 recomputes closure_kind from the evidence actually present, rejecting a uniform kind the evidence refutes (a `deductive` claim over a closure containing a Kani result is a G17 hard error). Optional and deliberately absent from the init template: a project that has not chosen an intent yet must not be silently defaulted to 'deductive'.

verifier_backends.description: plan.md §8.3 / chainlink #47 -- pluggable verifier dispatch, one command per verifier system, exactly as llm_backend is a pluggable one-shot command for Stage 0/3. `pipeline.py check-bridges` compiles a promoted bridge's bridge_logic to a harness and invokes the command for the verifier that owns the bridge's cluster, appending the generated harness path. The command must print one JSON verdict object on stdout: {result: pass|fail, scope, assumptions, config}. Optional and deliberately absent by default: with no backend configured, no bridge check is recorded and the gate blocks -- a verifier that never ran must never produce a pass, so the ceiling stays harness-tested (never bridge-checked).

command.description: Invocation, split on whitespace; the harness path is appended as the final argument.
Invocation, split on whitespace; the harness path is appended as the final argument.
Invocation, split on whitespace; the harness path is appended as the final argument.

witness_backend.description: plan.md §16.2 / chainlink #30 -- pluggable witness producer dispatch, one command, exactly as verifier_backends is pluggable dispatch for #47. `pipeline.py gate-g19` invokes this command fresh for every genuinely valid witness spec, appending --witness-id, --concept, --query, --fixture-id, --seed and --renderer taken from that spec's OWN current fields -- so a regenerated result's identity cannot silently disagree with what the spec currently declares, it was constructed from those exact values. The command must print one JSON canonical result object on stdout, matching docs/witness-result-schema.json (the same contract tests/fixtures/witnesses/stand_in_producer.py already implements). Optional and deliberately absent by default: with no backend configured, G19 cannot verify a determinism claim against an actual run and blocks -- a query that was never re-evaluated must never produce a pass.

command.description: Invocation, split on whitespace; --witness-id/--concept/--query/--fixture-id/--seed/--renderer are appended.

reliance_policy_path.description: plan.md §2 semantic policy doc, versioned governance -- not a one-time artifact.

witness_policy_path.description: plan.md §16.5 -- optional, only if the project declares feature witnesses.

write_set.description: The enforcement boundary for where the implementing agent may write (chainlink #77). Enforced read-only by `ligature write-set-check`: a file outside every allowed_roots pattern and not accounted for by protected_roots, the ownership manifest, a declared crate's specs/ tree, a canonical pipeline location, or the pinned upstream checkout is an out-of-set write, reported as a high-severity write-set finding in check --json and as status --json's write_set.state. A pattern matching every path (e.g. "**") or an empty protected_roots declares no boundary and is itself reported as a violation.

allowed_roots.description: Default allowed_write_set roots (plan.md §10) -- a starting point each work package narrows, never widens.

protected_roots.description: Default protected_write_set roots (plan.md §10) -- specs, CI manifests, gate scripts, schemas, policy docs, Cargo/build files, harnesses, toolchain pins. ENFORCED, not advisory (chainlink #103): a file inside one of these patterns and outside every allowed_roots pattern is a write into a protected root unless a declaration vouches for that specific file (the ownership manifest's managed set, a declared user-owned document, the ownership manifest itself, or a pipeline artifact the artifact system recognizes). A file inside a protected root the pipeline owns that the artifact system does not recognize is a `protected-write` violation -- blocking, exit 1, one high-severity write-set finding. A file inside a protected root the pipeline writes nothing into (a project's own Cargo.toml, .github/, scripts/) is reported in `protected_unvouched` and in `write-set-check --json`'s per-pattern `protected_surface`, non-blocking, because nothing in the workspace separates the project's file from an agent's; every declared pattern is reported with its file count, including one matching no file at all.

gate_integrity.description: Gate-implementation paths to hash-pin (G13 validates before any gate runs, plan.md §10/§12).

llm_backend.description: plan.md §6.1 -- pluggable one-shot LLM backend for Stage 0/3 and findings-driven re-entry.

kind.description: manual = print the constructed prompt and wait for the user to run it themselves and hand back the result.

command.description: Override the default invocation (e.g. a non-default claude -p flag set). Ignored when kind == 'manual'.

cluster_name.description: A cluster name, in the one form every other cluster-naming field in this pipeline already requires: docs/closure-profile-schema.json's `cluster` (which must equal the closure profile's own filename stem, G1b) and schemas/project-state.schema.json's `cluster`. Enforced here on `verifier_policy.clusters`' keys (chainlink #104) so a key that could not name a cluster in any artifact is refused at load rather than accepted as an override nothing will ever read.

verifier.description: The verifier systems this pipeline dispatches to: 'creusot' (deductive verification for Rust), 'verus' (deductive verification for Rust), 'kani' (model checking for Rust). Case-sensitive, exact match -- no composition ('verus+kani' is not a value; declare a second verifier under verifier_policy.supporting), no whitespace tolerance.
